newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up sharply, Dec sets new high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up sharply, Dec sets new high.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended up sharply Friday in a moderate session, with spot-December driven to a new contract high by technical buying after yesterday's strong rally, industry sources said.
December finished 12.1 cents higher at $2.908 per million British thermal units after hitting a new high of $2.94 earlier in the session. January settled up 9.5 cents at $2.883.

"There's no real weather to back this up, but short sellers are on the run and the next target looks like $3.10," said one Midwest trader, adding uncertainty over weather was likely to keep the bears cautious near-term.
Fundamental traders said the tendency to conserve storage early in the withdrawal season should keep the cash fairly buoyant near-term.

While chart traders agreed the market was clearly in an uptrend, some noted recent sharp gains in open interest on moves to the upside, meaning at some point the trend could be undermined by a flood of long liquidation.

Technically, traders said December's drive to a new high Friday was likely to lead to a test of next resistance at the June 28 spot continuation high of $2.98. Next resistance was seen at the spot highs in the $3.10 area seen in January. Support was pegged at $2.75 and then along the up trendline in the low-$2.60s.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices gained almost a nickel Friday to the mid-to-high $2.70s. Midwest pipes were up a similar amount to about $2.60. But New York city gate weekend gas tanked by 20-30 cents to the $3.40s on prospects for milder weather Monday.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rallied 5.2 cents to $2.293. NYMEX said 50,636 Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 44,734.

NYMEX December Alberta natgas was untraded but closed 4.5 cents lower at $1.605. Deferred contracts settled down by two to six cents. NYMEX said five Alberta contracts traded versus 23 lots on Thursday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the seventh consecutive day. December ended seven cents higher at $2.60.
On the KCBT, December finished up 12 cents at $2.715, while forwards settled one to 10 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 19.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
